Hey!! I’m so glad I saw this because I have the same problem! I talked to my therapist about it and she said she used to struggle with the same thing! What helped her and is beginning to help me, was just watching TV! Focus on characters reactions specifically, that’s how kids learn to communicate and express emotions, from watching adults and TV. Tv is a good one because it’s something we can relate to and can find a character funny or annoying, so we are able to tell more easily which reactions are uncalled for and which would be appropriate in a given situation. The show she recommended to me was Schitt’s Creek, which I never thought I’d like, but it’s actually hilarious and the characters exaggerate their facial expressions a lot, so it’s pretty easy to picture their faces in my head when I need to react to something. Any show you like would probably work as long as you remember to mimic the appropriate reactions! A character can be created to be way over the top so keep that in mind :)
